blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning Demystified: Preserving Neural Geometry During Model Adaptation
blogs.description: An introductory guide to Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), explaining why keeping pairwise neuron angles intact matters, how a learnable orthogonal matrix transforms pretrained weights, and what advantages this brings over standard finetuning.

blogs.title: The Parameter Bottleneck in Orthogonal Finetuning and How Block‑Diagonal Schemes Try to Solve It
blogs.description: A deep dive into why a full orthogonal matrix is expensive ($\mathcal{O}(d^2)$ parameters), the block‑diagonal trick used in original OFT to cut costs, and the expressiveness trade‑offs that come with fixed sparsity patterns.

blogs.title: Seeing Orthogonal Matrices as Information Networks: The Transmission Perspective
blogs.description: Explains the novel graph‑based view where building a dense orthogonal matrix equals transmitting information across a $d\times(m\!+\!1)$ grid. Visual examples show how sparsity patterns affect connectivity and guide efficient factorisations.

blogs.title: Butterfly Factorization 101: Turning Fast Fourier Tricks into Parameter‑Efficient Finetuning
blogs.description: Introduces butterfly structures from the Cooley–Tukey FFT algorithm, illustrates how they achieve dense connectivity with only $\mathcal{O}(d\log d)$ edges, and connects this insight to building sparse orthogonal factors for model adaptation.

blogs.title: Introducing Orthogonal Butterfly Fine‑tuning (BOFT): Combining Sparsity and Orthogonality
blogs.description: Walks through the BOFT method—multiplying several orthogonal butterfly components to create a dense orthogonal matrix, explains the $\mathcal{O}(d\log d)$ parameter budget, identity initialization, and the specially designed multiplicative dropout.

blogs.title: BOFT vs LoRA & Adapters: Which Parameter‑Efficient Strategy Wins?
blogs.description: A comparative study that pits BOFT against popular PEFT techniques such as LoRA, adapters and prompt tuning across vision transformers, large language models and diffusion models; highlights differences in performance stability and generalisation.

blogs.title: Why BOFT Generalizes Better: Theory of Expressivity, Spectral Norm Preservation & Inductive Bias
blogs.description: Summarises the theoretical foundations behind BOFT—its greater expressivity than block‑diagonal OFT (including the key theorem), preservation of spectral norms for stable training, and how butterfly structure injects useful inductive bias.

blogs.title: The Road Ahead for Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning: Limitations of BOFT & Emerging Network Topologies
blogs.description: Discusses current drawbacks like extra training runtime overhead, explores whether other network topologies from computer networking could beat butterflies for dense orthogonal construction, and outlines promising directions for future research.
